generation.explanation: At a fraction \(z/H\) of the way from the tip, a cone’s cross-sectional radius is \((z/H)R\), so its area is \(\pi R^2(z/H)^2\). Adding these cross-sectional areas from tip to base gives \(\frac13\pi R^2H\), while the cylinder has constant area \(\pi R^2\) throughout, so its volume is \(\pi R^2H\).
